P3894.corridor_notes: P3894 is GEM's 'Main Line Capacity Upgrade' of the parent Sakhalin-Khabarovsk-Vladivostok Gas Pipeline (P0758, operating, 1822 km, StartLocation 'Sakhalin Gas Compressor Station' / EndLocation 'Vladivostok'). LengthMergedKm=0.00 confirms no new pipe -- the 'route' is the existing 1,822 km trunk from GKS Sakhalin (Nogliki district, NE Sakhalin) via Komsomolsk-on-Amur and Khabarovsk to Vladivostok. The upgrade itself (also called Power of Siberia-3 in some coverage) is being delivered by reconstructing/adding compressor capacity at the head station GKS Sakhalin -- contractor SGK-1 (Gazstroyprom subsidiary), target completion 2024 per rusdevelopers.ru, raising throughput from 6 bcm/y (initial) toward the system's designed 30 bcm/y ceiling. No new above-ground route geometry is expected for a candidate route beyond the parent line's corridor.
P3894.researcher_notes: Parent GEM row identified as P0758 'Sakhalin-Khabarovsk-Vladivostok Gas Pipeline' (no SegmentName, operating, 1822.00 km, StartLocation 'Sakhalin Gas Compressor Station', EndLocation 'Vladivostok') -- exact match to this row's Start/EndProvince (Khabarovsk territory / Heilongjiang is odd for EndProvince given the pipeline never reaches China, but that's a pre-existing GEM field, not something this research resolved). Existing ResearcherNotes (NF 7/3/24) already flagged the 'Power of Siberia-3' alias and 2022 compressor-only expansion scope; this pass corroborates with rusdevelopers.ru (2024 reconstruction contract, 6->30 bcm/y target) and tn.spb.ru (GKS Sakhalin site description, 32 MW, 10 km N of Val). Route geometry for a candidate geojson should reuse/reference P0758's route if one exists in the routes repo, not be redrawn from scratch.
P3894.blockers: Exact coordinates for GKS Sakhalin (the actual compressor station pad, not the Val village anchor) and for the Vladivostok-side gas distribution station were not found in open sources -- Russian govt/Gazprom technical filings with precise siting were not accessible. Wikimapia has a pinned location for GKS Sakhalin but the page is JS-rendered and coordinates could not be extracted via WebFetch.

P5079.corridor_notes: No dedicated source for a Wudalianchi-Nenjiang gas pipeline branch was found despite targeted Chinese-language searches (both cities are ~110 km apart in Heihe prefecture, Heilongjiang). This corroborates the existing GEM ResearcherNotes ('Q3 2025: There is still no relevant information'). Two adjacent/similarly-named projects exist but are confirmed NOT this pipeline: (1) a 195 km 'Nenjiang branch' (嫩江支线) of the China-Russia East Line running Fuyu distribution station -> Nenjiang terminal station, crossing Fuyu County, Nehe City and Nenjiang City (construction started 2023-09-20) -- this starts at Fuyu, not Wudalianchi; (2) a Wudalianchi COMPRESSOR STATION (五大连池压气站) on the China-Russia East Line's Heihe-Changling mainline trunk itself (Phase-2 pressure boost, tested/ready per PipeChina 2025 announcement) -- this is a station on the trunk, not a Wudalianchi-Nenjiang branch pipeline.
P5079.researcher_notes: Status is cancelled and LengthMergedKm is '--' (blank/unknown) in GEM, consistent with a project that may never have reached a public planning stage with its own documentation. Searched multiple query variants ('五大连池 讷河 天然气管道', '中俄东线 五大连池-讷河 环评', quoted-phrase combos) via DuckDuckGo -- returned only unrelated road-bridge tenders and unrelated pipeline projects (see corridor_notes). Endpoint coordinates given are city-center geocodes of the two named places in the GEM segment name only, NOT sourced to any document describing this pipeline -- per instructions this keeps resolution at PARTIAL despite having lon/lat.
P5079.blockers: No verifiable ref found for this specific branch's existence, route, or endpoints beyond the GEM row's own segment name. Recommend re-checking closer to any future Heihe-prefecture gas infrastructure announcements, or asking whether 'Wudalianchi-Nenjiang' might actually be a mis-scoped/renamed duplicate of the confirmed Fuyu-Nenjiang branch (different start point) -- worth a cross-check against that GEM row if one exists.

P6805.corridor_notes: Official project name: 中俄东线明哈支线天然气管道绥北支线工程 (China-Russia East Line Minghar-branch gas pipeline, Suibei branch project), built by PetroChina Kunlun Gas & Electric. Runs due west-to-east ~9 km (matches GEM LengthMergedKm=9.00) from the existing Suihua terminal station (tie-in 2m outside its perimeter wall) to a new Suibei terminal station, Beilin District, Suihua City. Pipe D219.1mm, design pressure 6.3MPa, design capacity 65 million m3/yr. Two stations built along the route: 绥北清管站 (Suibei pigging station, unmanned) and 绥北末站 (Suibei terminal station, manned). Crosses the Suibei Expressway once (bored) and 8 rural roads. A 2024 Suihua government work report confirms 'opened the China-Russia gas pipeline Suihua branch' (开通中俄天然气管道绥化支线), consistent with commissioning in 2023.
P6805.researcher_notes: GEM's existing StartLocation 'Suihua' / EndLocation 'Suibei' map exactly onto the official project's 绥化末站 (start) / 绥北末站 (end) -- strong confirmation this is the right project. The primary ref is a PDF (2022 EIA public-participation notice, PetroChina Kunlun Gas & Electric) -- resolves 200 but url_verifier's content screen doesn't reliably extract the embedded Chinese text (a known false-negative class per the verifier's own docs), so I read it directly with pdftotext -layout and confirmed the exact station names, DMS coordinates, and 9km length quoted above match GEM's row. The suihua.gov.cn government work-report source has a broken TLS cert chain (SSLError on direct fetch, matches the verifier's documented false-negative class) -- cited via a working web.archive.org snapshot instead, which the verifier passed with content match.

P6806.corridor_notes: P6806 'Mingshui Branch' (明水支线) is confirmed as a project DISTINCT from the already-operating Mingshui-Harbin Branch (明水-哈尔滨支线, GEM P5062, 171.23 km, commissioned 2020-10-31). Suihua municipal government's June 2024 '14th Five-Year Plan carbon-intensity reduction' implementation notice (绥政发〔2024〕15号) explicitly lists both as separate line items to advance: '...依托中俄东线天然气管道干线、中俄东线天然气管线（明水-哈尔滨）支线，积极推进绥北支线、明水支线、肇东-肇东经济开发区-兰西支线等各条支线建设' (relying on the China-Russia East Line trunk and the Mingshui-Harbin branch, actively advance construction of the Suibei branch, MINGSHUI BRANCH, and the Zhaodong-Zhaodong Economic Development Zone-Lanxi branch, among others). This confirms 明水支线 as a real, separately-tracked line still under construction as of mid-2024, matching GEM's 'construction' status. GEM's LengthMergedKm (177.00) exceeds the entire existing Mingshui-Harbin line's length (171.23 km to Harbin, further than just to Suihua), which suggests this new branch may follow a different/longer alignment rather than simply paralleling the existing corridor -- flagged as an open question, not resolved by available sources.
P6806.researcher_notes: The bjx.com.cn URL already on this row (from MZ's prior pass) resolves (200) but is behind an Aliyun WAF CAPTCHA that blocked both WebFetch and a Jina-reader proxy from reading its content -- I could not independently verify it says what MZ's note claims. I located and read the primary source directly instead: the Suihua municipal government's own June 2024 carbon-plan notice (via a working web.archive.org snapshot, since suihua.gov.cn direct-fetch fails with a broken TLS cert chain, a documented url_verifier false-negative class), which independently confirms '明水支线' as a real, distinct, still-under-construction branch. No source gives exact route/townships for this branch beyond the county-level Mingshui start and the shared Suihua terminal-station end (same 绥化末站 as P6805/明哈支线) -- coordinates are therefore county/station-anchor level, not a sourced corridor.
P6806.blockers: Exact alignment/townships crossed and why the length (177 km) exceeds the full Mingshui-Harbin line's length could not be resolved from available sources -- worth a follow-up search once more construction-phase reporting (EIA public notices, tender announcements) becomes available for this specific line, the way it did for the Suibei branch (P6805).

P7633.corridor_notes: Official PipeChina EIA public-participation notices (1st, 2nd, 3rd rounds, 2025-2026) give the route in GEM's own words verbatim: '管道起自中俄东线大庆联络站，终点为长春—石家庄管道长岭联络站' (pipeline begins at the Daqing liaison station of the China-Russia East Line, ends at the Changling liaison station of the Changchun-Shijiazhuang pipeline). Total length ~196.8-202 km (matches GEM LengthMergedKm=202.00). Route: Heilongjiang segment ~88-92.5 km through Zhaozhou County then Zhaoyuan County (both Daqing prefecture); Jilin segment ~108.7-109.5 km entirely within Qian Gorlos Mongol Autonomous County, Songyuan City. Pipe diameter D1219mm, design pressure 12MPa, design capacity 48 bcm/y. 3 station sites (all expansions of existing facilities) and 5 valve rooms along the route. As of the March 2026 3rd public notice the project was still in EIA public-comment phase (proposed), consistent with GEM's 'proposed' status. This is the connector linking the China-Russia East Line network (at Daqing) to the separate Changchun-Shijiazhuang trunk (at Changling) -- i.e. it is NOT part of either trunk's own branch family, but a standalone tie-line between the two systems.
P7633.researcher_notes: GEM's own StartLocation/EndLocation for this row are already the exact official station names in Chinese ('中俄东线大庆联络站' / '长春-石家庄管道长岭联络站'), which I confirmed word-for-word against three successive PipeChina official public notices (2025-03, 2025-xx 2nd round, 2026-03 3rd round) -- strong, well-corroborated match. None of the three notices publish station-level GPS coordinates, so endpoints are geocoded to city/county-seat level (Daqing city; Changling county seat) rather than the exact liaison-station pads. The route crosses Zhaozhou County first, then Zhaoyuan County, before the Jilin border -- so the true Daqing liaison-station site is more likely within Zhaozhou County than Daqing's urban core; flagged as an approximation.

P7720.corridor_notes: Official project: 中俄东线聊城支线 (China-Russia East Line Liaocheng branch). Route confirmed by a June 2025 news report on the site-selection public notice: begins at the Dezhou liaison station in Baizhuang Village, Wucheng County (Dezhou), ends at the Guguantun terminal station, Dongchangfu District (Liaocheng) -- total length ~142 km (matches GEM LengthMergedKm=143.50). Crosses, in order: Wucheng County -> Xiajin County (both Dezhou) -> Linqing City -> Chaiping District -> Dongchangfu District (all Liaocheng). Infrastructure includes pipeline, valve chambers, distribution stations and the terminal station. As of the May 2025 notice the project was in 'site-selection pre-approval public notice' phase, consistent with GEM's 'proposed' status. Multiple further procedural notices (Shandong provincial cultural-heritage clearance, land-conservation expert review, feasibility-study tender) corroborate the project is actively moving through China's project-approval pipeline as of 2025.
P7720.researcher_notes: GEM's existing StartLocation 'Baizhuang Village' / EndLocation 'Dongchangfu' are corroborated exactly by this independent qq.com report, which additionally supplies the county-by-county route (Wucheng -> Xiajin -> Linqing -> Chaiping -> Dongchangfu) and the precise station names (Dezhou liaison station / Guguantun terminal station) that GEM's row doesn't carry. The row's existing toutiao.com ref (Q3 2025 note) could not be read -- toutiao's app-only rendering returns empty content to both url_verifier's extractor and WebFetch -- so it is NOT included in the output refs; the qq.com source is an equally strong (likely syndicated-from-the-same-wire) independent substitute that passed url_verifier cleanly.
